College]] | nationality = | occupation = {{hlist|[[Actor]]|[[Model (person)|Model]]}} | years_active = 2005–2015 | spouse = {{marriage|Anupam Pandey|1997}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/nation/story/20090629-the-shine-wears-off-740063-2009-06-18|title=The shine wears off|first1=Swati|last1=Mathur|first2=Kaveree|last2=Bamzai|date=June 18, 2009|website=India Today}} | children = 1 | relatives = | website = }} '''Shiney Suraj Ahuja''' (born 15 May 1973) is an Indian former actor who worked in [[Hindi cinema|Hindi films]]. He won the [[Filmfare Award for Best Male Debut|Filmfare Best Male Debut Award]] for ''[[Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi]]'' in 2006 and then followed with several hit films like ''[[Gangster (2006 film)|Gangster]]'', ''[[Woh Lamhe]]'', ''[[Life in a Metro]]'', ''[[Bhool Bhulaiyaa]]'', and [[Welcome Back (film)|''Welcome Back'']]. == Early life and education == Ahuja was born on 15 May 1973 into a [[Punjabis|Punjabi]] family.{{cite web |author=Princy Jain |date=September 18, 2006 |title=I am a true Punjabi : Shiney |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/i-am-a-true-punjabi-shiney/story-4FwBwPBl9OzJiZaYM24SaN.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221211095959/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/i-am-a-true-punjabi-shiney/story-4FwBwPBl9OzJiZaYM24SaN.html |archive-date=December 11, 2022 |access-date=December 11, 2022 |publisher=[[Hindustan Times]] |language=en-IN}} His mother is from [[Shimla]], with her family originally from [[Sargoda]], and his father Suraj Ahuja's ancestry is from [[Sahiwal]], both in modern day [[Pakistan]].{{cite web |date=February 22, 2008 |author=Khalid Mohamed|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/i-m-no-marriage-thief-shiney-ahuja/story-Mp3wdXt7mWIfheRiKMK0QP.html|access-date=June 27, 2023 |title=I'm no marriage thief: Shiney Ahuja|publisher=[[Hindustan Times]] |language=en-IN}} His father was born in [[Dehradun]], and was a colonel in the [[Indian Army]]. Ahuja studied at [[St. Xavier's Senior Secondary School, Delhi]] and [[Army Public School, Dhaula Kuan]], before attending [[Hansraj College]] of the [[University of Delhi]], followed by [[R.V. College of Engineering]] in [[Bangalore]]. Later, he joined the theatre group "TAG" where he met [[Barry John (theatre director)|Barry John]]. Shortly thereafter, he joined John's acting school in Delhi.{{cite news|title=Wishing Shiney Ahuja a very happy Birthday|url=https://www.screenindia.com/news/wishing-shiney-ahuja-a-very-happy-birthday/459935/|work=[[Screen (magazine)|Screen]]|date=May 15, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090620055926/http://www.screenindia.com/news/wishing-shiney-ahuja-a-very-happy-birthday/459935/|archive-date=20 June 2009|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} == Career == After completing college, Ahuja featured in commercials for [[Pepsi]], [[Cadburys]], and [[Citibank]]. He also featured in the music video 'Pyar Ho Gaya' for the British-Asian band "[[Stereo Nation]]".{{Cite web |title=Hindi Song Pyar Ho Gaya Sung By Sterio Nation Feat. Shiney Ahuja |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/entertainment/music/hindi/hindi-song-pyar-ho-gaya-sung-by-sterio-nation-feat-shiney-ahuja/videoshow/65037126.cms |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=The Times of India |language=en}} [[Sudhir Mishra]], the director of ''[[Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi]]'', saw Shiney in the Pepsi commercial and called him to audition for [[Kay Kay Menon]]'s character – Sidharth Tyabji. Upon his request, Mishra also auditioned him for the role of Vikram Malhotra. He was selected from over 200 aspirants for the role of Vikram Malhotra and made his acting debut in the film.{{Citation needed|date= July 2022}} The film went on to win critical acclaim, and was screened at as many as 12 film festivals over 6 months. These included film festivals at [[Turkey]], [[Estonia]], River to River ([[Florence]]), [[Berlin]], [[Edinburgh]], [[Washington, D.C.|Washington]], [[Dallas]], [[India]] ([[Goa]]), Bite The Mango festival ([[Bradford]], [[United Kingdom|UK]]), the Commonwealth festival ([[Manchester]]), and the Pacific Rim festival ([[California]]).{{Citation needed|date= July 2022|reason=for film festivals}} The film was released commercially in 2005 with minimal publicity but a national footprint across India.{{Cite web |date=2025-04-16 |title=20 years of Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi {{!}} The film crossed the test of time, says writer and director Sudhir Mishra |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/htcity/cinema/20-years-of-hazaaron-khwaishein-aisi-the-film-crossed-the-test-of-time-says-writer-and-director-sudhir-mishra-101744722056864.html |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}} He received several Best Actor for Male Debut awards given for the year including the [[Filmfare Award for Best Male Debut#2000s|Filmfare Award for Best Male Debut]], [[Zee Cine Award for Best Male Debut]], and [[Stardust Award for Breakthrough Performance – Male|Stardust Award for Breakthrough Performance]].{{cite web| title=Filmfare winners of the year 2006 {{!}} Best Newcomer (Male)| access-date=9 December 2022| url=https://www.filmfare.com/awards/filmfare-awards/winners| website=filmfare.com}}{{Citation needed|date= July 2022|reason=for the several awards}} Thereafter, Ahuja played the lead role in [[Mahesh Bhatt]]'s ''[[Gangster (2006 film)|Gangster]]'', a popular commercial movie genre and ''[[Woh Lamhe]]'' opposite [[Kangana Ranaut]]. Other films followed including ''[[Life in a Metro]]'', ''[[Bhool Bhulaiyaa]]''. Two of his films, ''Ek Accident'' with co-star [[Soha Ali Khan]] and ''[[Har Pal]]'' with [[Preity Zinta]] are yet to be released.{{cite news|url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/141125/entertainment-bollywood/article/producers-refused-account-har-pal-following-shiney-ahuja-rape|title=Producers refused to account 'Har Pal' following Shiney Ahuja rape case, reveals Jahnu Barua|work=Deccan Chronicle|publisher=Deccan Chronicle Holdings Limited|date=25 November 2014|access-date=31 January 2015}} In 2015, Ahuja was cast in [[Anees Bazmee]]'s ''[[Welcome Back (film)|Welcome Back]]'' co-starring [[John Abraham (actor)|John Abraham]], [[Shruti Hassan]], [[Anil Kapoor]], [[Nana Patekar]], [[Naseeruddin Shah]], [[Dimple Kapadia]] and [[Paresh Rawal]].{{cite web|url=http://www.bollywoodlife.com/news-gossip/john-abraham-shruti-haasan-and-shiney-ahuja-strike-a-pose-on-the-sets-of-welcome-back-view-pics/#!1/teaser-welcome-back-1-101014/|access-date=18 January 2015|title=John Abraham, Shruti Haasan, and Shiney Ahuja strike a pose on the sets of Welcome Back-view pics! – Bollywood News & Gossip, Movie Reviews, Trailers & Videos at Bollywoodlife.com|date=10 October 2014 }}{{Cite news |date=2014-09-05 |title=Shiney Ahuja returns as Naseer's son |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/Shiney-Ahuja-returns-as-Naseers-son/articleshow/41766225.cms |access-date=2025-10-05 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}} As of 2025, ''Welcome Back'' was his last released movie, and he was said to be living in the [[Philippines]], working as a garment shop owner.{{Cite web |last=Palat |first=Lakshana N. |date=2025-10-29 |title=Bollywood to prison to Philippines: The story of Shiney Ahuja |url=https://gulfnews.com/entertainment/from-bollywood-star-to-jail-and-now-rumoured-philippine-garment-shop-owner-shiney-ahujas-story-1.500325774 |access-date=2026-07-03 |website=[[Gulf News]] |language=en}} ==Personal life == Ahuja is married to Anupam Pande, and they have a daughter Arshiya.{{cite web| title=Exclusive: My Daughter Is My Biggest Strength, Says Shiney Ahuja| author=Priyanka Jain| date=2 September 2015| url=https://www.thequint.com/entertainment/exclusive-my-daughter-is-my-biggest-strength-says-shiney-ahuja| website=thequint.com}}{{cite web| title=Life will go back to normal again: Shiney's wife| url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/life-will-go-back-to-normal-again-shineys-wife/articleshow/8911291.cms| date=20 June 2011| author=Sarita Tanwar| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150723092840/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/life-will-go-back-to-normal-again-shineys-wife/articleshow/8911291.cms |archive-date=23 July 2015 |website=indiatimes.com}}{{Cite web |title=Who is Shiney Ahuja's wife, Anupam Pande? She stood with her husband during rape trial, quit high paying job |url=https://www.india.com/entertainment/meet-shiney-ahujas-wife-who-left-her-dream-job-for-him-defended-him-during-rape-cases-allegations-her-name-is-7938218/ |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=www.india.com |language=en}} == Legal issues == In June 2009, Ahuja was arrested on charges of raping, detaining, and threatening his 19-year-old domestic servant. He was booked under Section 376 (rape), and Section 506 (threat to kill) of the [[Indian Penal Code]].{{Cite web |date=15 May 2020 |title=Remember Shiney Ahuja? The Gangster actor is completely away from the limelight |url=https://www.mid-day.com/entertainment/bollywood-news/photo/Remember-Shiney-Ahuja-The-Gangster-actor-is-completely-away-from-limelight-84384#4 |accessdate=30 July 2021 |website=[[Mid Day]]}} During the trial, his maid (the victim) recanted on her testimony and told the Court that she was never raped. However, the judge believed that the maid falsely testified under pressure and, in 2011, Ahuja was sentenced to seven years of prison.{{Cite web|url=http://www.theguardian.com/world/2011/mar/31/shiney-ahuja-bollywood-jailed-raping|title=Shiney Ahuja, fallen Bollywood star, jailed for raping maid|date=31 March 2011|website=The Guardian}}{{Cite news |date=2011-03-31 |title=Indian actor Shiney Ahuja jailed in rape case |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-south-asia-12916886 |access-date=2025-10-05 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}} This case was the inspiration for the writing of the legal drama film ''[[Section 375]]''. The film was written by [[Manish Gupta (director)|Manish Gupta]], his friend who had interacted with the parties of the case during the time of the arrest.{{cite web| url=https://www.thequint.com/entertainment/bollywood/section-375-writer-talks-about-how-the-shiney-ahuja-case-inspired-the-film#read-more| title=Shiney Ahuja Case Inspired 'Section 375', Says Film's Writer|date=17 Sep 2019| accessdate=30 Jul 2021| author=Nandakumar Rammohan| website=thequint.com}}{{cite web| url=https://www.ibtimes.co.in/section-375-story-based-shiney-ahujas-rape-case-reveals-writer-manish-gupta-805587| title=Section 375 story is based on Ahuja's rape case, reveals writer Manish Gupta| date=September 17, 2019| accessdate=30 Jul 2021| author=Suparno Sarkar| website=ibtimes.co.in}}{{Cite web |last= |first= |last2= |first2= |date=2025-05-15 |title=Did Shiney Ahuja's rape case inspire Akshaye Khanna, Richa Chadha's Section 375 story? extract: Shiney Suraj Ahuja (born 15 May 1973) is an Indian former actor who worked in Hindi films. He won the Filmfare Best Male Debut Award for Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi in 2006 and then followed with several hit films like Gangster, Woh Lamhe, Life in a Metro, Bhool Bhulaiyaa, and Welcome Back.
